Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to the UTI Asset 
Management Company Limited Q2 and H1 FY '27 Earnings Conference 
Call. From the management, we have with us Mr. Vinay Lakhotia, Chief 
Financial Officer and Head of Corporate Strategy; and Mr. Sandeep 
Samsi, Head of Investor Experience and Corporate Affairs. We also have 
the Investor Relations team from Adfactors PR.  
 
As a reminder, all participant lines will be in listen-only mode. There will 
be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation 
concludes. Should you need any assistance during this conference, 
please signal for an operator by pressing star followed by zero on your 
touchtone telephone.  
 
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Sandeep Samsi for opening 
remarks. Thank you, and over to you, sir. 
Sandeep Samsi: 
Thank you, Farah. Good evening, everyone, and thank you for joining us 
today. Due to an urgent family exigency, Mr. Vetri Subramaniam, our MD 
and CEO, will not be able to join today's earnings call. I have Mr. Vinay 
Lakhotia, CFO, and Head of Corporate Strategy, along with me on this 
call.  
 
Our financial results for the quarter and half year ended 30th September 
2026, along with the investor presentation and press release, have been 
shared on the stock exchanges as well as on our website, and we trust 
you had the opportunity to review them.  
 
Before we discuss our financial performance, I would like to cover three 
key areas. First, the macroeconomic environment and the broader 
mutual fund industry backdrop; secondly, the progress we have made 
against our strategic priorities during quarter two of FY '27 and in the first 
half of the financial year; and finally, why we remain confident in UTI 
AMC's long-term growth trajectory and opportunities ahead. 
 
Speaking on the macroeconomic environment, quarter two of FY '27 
witnessed resilient domestic activity, with quarter one GDP growth at 
7.8%, supported by manufacturing and services sectors. However, West

Asia tensions and crude oil volatility heightened inflationary pressures, 
with retail inflation rising to 5.54% in September '26. This month, the RBI 
also raised the repo rate to 5.50% and projected FY '27 GDP growth at 
7.1%.  
 
Despite quarter-end market volatility, domestic investors' participation 
remained resilient. Equity-oriented schemes attracted Rs. 92,333 crores 
in quarter two of FY '27, taking the first half FY '27 inflows to Rs. 1.83 lakh 
crores. In September '26, the equity inflows stood at Rs. 38,307 crores, 
while the monthly SIP contribution reached a record Rs. 32,490 crores, 
with the SIP AUM being at Rs. 17.86 lakh crores for industry. 
 
Small and mid-cap funds accounted for 44% of September's equity 
inflows, while flexi-cap, multi-cap, large and mid-cap, and large-cap 
funds accounted  another 41%. Industry quarterly average AUM rose to 
Rs. 87.2 lakh crores from Rs. 83.1 lakh crores in quarter one of FY '27, with 
ETFs recording net inflows of Rs. 15,501 crores in September '26. 
 
For UTI, the underlying message is encouraging. Even though short-term 
volatility is an inherent part of equity investing, the structural drivers of the 
mutual fund industry, including the economic growth, rising income, 
broader investor participation, and financialisation of household savings, 
remain intact.  
 
Keeping these opportunities in mind, our focus remains on translating the 
industry's structural growth potential into substantial growth for UTI AMC 
and capturing a larger share of industry flows.  
Under our Mission 2031, we are looking to work across five 
interconnected priorities:  
 
• 
Accelerating AUM growth,  
• 
Strengthening our SIP  franchise,  
• 
Expanding distribution reach,  
• 
Deepening digital capabilities, and  
• 
Delivering better outcomes for investors.

Turning to our business performance, our mutual fund quarterly average 
AUM for quarter two of FY '27 stood at Rs. 4.02 lakh crores, compared with 
Rs. 3.93 lakh crores in quarter one of FY '27, representing a market share 
of 4.61%. Our total group AUM stood at Rs. 16.28 lakh crores as of 
September 30th, 2026.  
 
Equity-oriented assets across active and passive strategies accounted 
for 72% of our average mutual fund AUM, compared with approximately 
70% in the previous quarter. Our SIP franchise remains resilient, with 
combined monthly SIP and STP inflows standing at Rs. 982 crores in 
September of '26. 
 
Our SIP AUM stood at Rs. 45,572 crores as of September 30, 2026, broadly 
stable as compared with Rs. 45,595 crores in June of '26. This reinforces 
our focus on systematic investment as a driver of sustainable growth. The 
gross SIP inflows were Rs. 2,583 crores during this quarter and Rs. 5,085 
crores during the half year of FY '27.  
 
Furthermore, we registered 5.96 lakh new SIPs during quarter two of FY 
'27, of which 87% were sourced through digital channels. In quarter two 
of FY '27, our live folio base stood at 1.47 crores, and we added  3.6 lakh 
new investors as identified by their PAN. During the half year, we added  
6.12 lakh investors. 
 
UTI Mutual Fund's share of industry's new SIP registration by volume 
stood at 4.08% in quarter two. This is an encouraging indicator of our 
efforts to improve participation in new business. The next step is to build 
on this momentum consistently, strengthen conversions across 
distribution channels and digital platforms, and translate new investor 
acquisition into sustained SIP contribution and long-term partnerships. 
 
On the financial performance: on the financial front, the consolidated 
core revenue from the sale of services stood at Rs. 398 crores for quarter 
two of FY27, compared to Rs. 390 crores in the corresponding quarter last 
year, while the core profit after tax was Rs. 131 crores.

For H1 of FY27, core revenues stood at Rs. 777 crores and core profit after 
tax at Rs. 263 crores. Our focus remains on growing the business while 
maintaining operating discipline and ensuring that growth translates into 
sustainable profitability. On strengthening investment capabilities and 
product propositions, the quality of our investment outcomes is 
highlighted through our experienced team, renewed talent base and 
stronger client-facing capabilities.  
Our proprietary framework, the Score Alpha for equities and GIMS  
framework for fixed income, brings discipline to research, portfolio 
construction and risk management across market cycles. These  
capabilities are reflected in the depth of our research and investment 
evaluation.  
During the first half of FY27, our equity research coverage expanded to 
480 companies. We evaluated 36 IPOs and participated in six, while 
continuing to invest in research infrastructure and talent. These  efforts 
deepen our understanding of business, strengthen investment decisions 
and support better outcomes for investors over the long term. 
On our equity scheme performance, several of our funds have 
demonstrated an improvement in performance over the last quarter, with 
51% of our equity and hybrid funds ranked in quartile one or quartile two 
on a three-month basis as of September '26. While on our fixed income 
schemes, 97% of our AUM, including liquid funds, were in the top two 
quartiles over a 3-month period, while 61% was in the top two quartiles 
over a 1-year period, reflecting performance of our fund management 
capabilities across different investment horizons. 
We broadened our product offering across active and passive strategies. 
During quarter two of FY27, we launched the UTI Balanced Hybrid Fund 
and four passive products linked to the Nifty 500 and BSE India Sector 
Leaders indices. Our Nifty 500 Index Fund and the BSE India Sector 
Leader Index Fund established encouraging positions within the 
respective categories.

These developments expand the range of products available to our 
investors and distributors while strengthening our capability to 
participate across investment needs and market segments. Going 
forward, the focus will be on building awareness, improving product 
reach, and ensuring that product innovation contributes meaningfully to 
sustainable business growth. 
On our additional growth engines, building diversified growth engines 
remains an important pillar of our long-term strategy. We have received 
SEBI approval for our Specialised Investment Fund - SIF initiative and will 
be launching the UTI Classif  Hybrid Long Short Fund in quarter three of 
FY27.  
In our alternatives business, the first investment for the late-stage private 
equity fund was signed, while SDOF IV crossed Rs. 1,000 crores. Our 
pension fund onboarded 169 new corporates between April '26 and 
October '26 and our international business continued to pursue product 
initiatives across markets, including the US, Singapore, UAE and GIFT 
City.  
These  initiatives broaden our opportunity set beyond the core mutual 
fund franchise. Expanding the distribution and strengthening the digital 
capabilities are the key to capturing a larger share of the industry growth. 
During the quarter two of FY27, 80.30% of our mutual fund AUM was 
contributed by the top 30 cities, while B30 accounted for 19.7% of the 
AUM.  
We onboarded ten new Fintech partners and continued building digital 
infrastructure while advancing data analytics and automation to simplify 
investor journeys, improving investor service efficiency and strengthening 
conversion. Our fintech partners facilitated approximately 1 lakh 
transactions during the quarter two of FY27 and these partners have 
contributed 67% of the new investor acquisitions. 
Operating efficiency remains the key to scaling our business. Process 
optimisation generated approximately Rs. 4.22 crores in savings, while 
automation is reducing manual intervention. As we invest in talent,

maintaining cost discipline and strengthening operating leverage. 
Our people remain central to our Mission 2031 initiative. We continue to 
invest in the organisational capability, with 10,690 training hours 
delivered to the sales team up to September of '26, while strengthening 
performance management and identifying critical talent for development 
and retention.

performance of the company in greater detail.

follows, beginning with the performance of quarter two.  
On a standalone basis, the core income, which is the sale of service, 
amounted to Rs. 324 crores, up by 2% Y-o-Y and 5% Q-o-Q.  
The core profit after tax for the quarter is Rs. 136 crores, up by 31% Y-o-Y 
and 14% Q-o-Q. The profit after tax stood at Rs. 143 crores, down by 14% 
Y-o-Y and 34% Q-o-Q.  
On a consolidated basis, the core income, i.e. the sale of service 
amounted to Rs. 398 crores, up by 2% Y-o-Y and 5% Q-o-Q. The core profit 
after tax for the quarter is Rs. 131 crores, up by 22% Y-o-Y and 2% Q-o-Q. 
The profit after tax stood at Rs. 132 crores, up by 17% Y-o-Y and down by 
55% Q-o-Q. 
For the half year of FY27, the standalone core income amounted to Rs. 
632 crores, up by 1% Y-o-Y. The core profit after tax for the half year is Rs. 
253 crores, up by 14% Y-o-Y. The profit after tax stood at Rs. 361 crores, 
down by 5% Y-o-Y.  
On a consolidated basis, the core income amounted to Rs. 777 crores, up 
by 1% Y-o-Y. The core profit after tax for H1 FY27 is Rs. 263 crores, up by 
15% Y-o-Y. The profit after tax stood at Rs. 426 crores, up by 22% Y-o-Y.

For UTI Pension Fund Limited, our 100% owned subsidiary, UTI Pension 
Fund has recorded a year-on-year growth of approximately 10.97% in its 
AUM, reaching approximately Rs. 4.32 lakh crores as on 30th September 
2026, as compared to Rs. 3.89 lakh crores as on 30th September 2025. It 
currently manages approximately 24.01% of the NPS industry's AUM. 
UTI International, which represents our international business, has an 
AUM of USD1.67 billion, which is approximately Rs. 16,063 crores as on 
30th September 2026. Our international clients are spread across more 
than 30 countries and are primarily institutions, pensions, insurance 
companies, banks, and asset managers. 
UTI International is actively exploring strategic partnership opportunities 
with leading asset managers in key international markets, including East 
Asia and Latin America, as part of its broader strategy to strengthen its 
global distribution network, expand its international presence, and 
enhance access to Indian investment opportunities for investors 
worldwide. 
UTI Alternatives' AUM has grown to approximately Rs. 4,045 crores, up 
52% from Rs. 2,669 crores as on September of 2025. This AUM represents 
commitment for funds in the commitment period and net capital for funds 
in the post-commitment period. It also includes the co-investment 
portfolio managed by UTI Alternatives.  
UTI SDOF IV has crossed the Rs. 1,000 crores milestone. Launched in 
quarter three of FY26 as the fourth fund in our SDOF series, the fund is 
planned as a Rs. 1,500 crores with a greenshoe option of Rs. 500 crores. 
It already has reached an AUM of Rs. 1,131 crores and is currently in 
raising and investing stage.  
UTI Alternatives currently manages six active domestic funds across 
performing credit and multi-strategy themes, along with two GIFT City 
feeder funds. UTI Multi-Opportunity Fund I has an AUM of approximately 
Rs. 1,599 crores as of September '26 and is currently in investing stage. 
UTI Multi-Opportunity Fund II has a total commitment of Rs. 359 crores as 
of September and is currently in raising and investing stage.

As we enter the second half of FY27, our priorities are clear: improve our 
participation in industry flows, strengthen our SIP franchise, deepen 
distribution productivity, maintain competitive investment capabilities, 
and build greater efficiency into our operations. Mission 2031 provides 
the direction. Our task is to translate that direction into sustained flows in 
AUM and inflows, stronger profitability, and better outcomes for our 
investors.  
With this, we would like to open the forum for question-and-answer 
session. Thank you.
